title: 🚨 YOUR MARRIAGE PROBLEM MAY NOT BE WHAT YOU THINK IT IS.
paragraphs: 🚨 YOUR MARRIAGE PROBLEM MAY NOT BE WHAT YOU THINK IT IS.
You can pray together.
Go to church together.
Post Bible verses online.
And still quietly struggle with intimacy, communication, unmet expectations, and frustration inside your marriage.
Many Christian couples are suffering in silence because nobody taught them what God's Word actually says about intimacy, covenant love, and serving one another in marriage.
So they learn from culture.
Movies.
Social media.
Friends.
And then wonder why their marriage feels disconnected.
How We Should Handle the Sexual Needs of Our Partners Biblically
This is not a worldly relationship book.
This is a practical, Scripture-based guide designed to help Christian husbands and wives understand God's design for intimacy, love, respect, communication, and covenant faithfulness.
Because intimacy was God's idea before the world corrupted it.
🔥 WHY THIS BOOK MATTERS
Too many believers have been taught one of two extremes:
❌ Treat intimacy as shameful
OR
❌ Treat intimacy as selfish gratification
God's Word teaches something better.
A Christ-centered view of marriage that produces unity, trust, and deeper connection.
Inside this powerful guide you'll discover:
✅ What the Bible actually teaches about sexual needs in marriage
✅ How husbands and wives can serve one another biblically
✅ The biggest intimacy killers destroying Christian marriages
✅ How to communicate needs without conflict and resentment
✅ How to protect your marriage from pornography, temptation, and emotional distance
✅ What 1 Corinthians 7 really means for married couples
✅ How intimacy can become an act of love, service, and worship instead of frustration
✅ Practical biblical principles for building a stronger marriage
⚔️ MOST PEOPLE VS FEW PEOPLE
Most people learn about intimacy from culture.
Few people learn about intimacy from Scripture.
Most people want a better marriage.
Few people are willing to grow into a better spouse.
Most people focus on what they're not receiving.
Few people focus on how they can love like Christ.
Most people seek comfort.
Few people pursue covenant.
Which one are you?
